Shadowfax vs Delhivery: Which Logistics Stock Is Better Positioned for Growth After Q2FY27 Results?
India’s logistics demand is supporting both companies, with Shadowfax reporting 56.6% revenue growth and Rs. 68 crore profit, while Delhivery posted 22.1% transport revenue growth and Rs. 41 crore profit in Q2FY27.

The logistics industry of India is experiencing increasing demand from e-commerce, quick commerce, D2C, and organised retail. The increasing focus of companies on fast delivery and broader distribution networks is leading logistics providers to enhance their infrastructure and technology investments. In this context, Shadowfax and Delhivery witnessed growth in terms of revenues and operations in Q2 FY27, but the drivers of growth and company profiles of both differ from each other.

Shadowfax has been witnessing fast growth in terms of express logistics, quick commerce, and D2C logistics, whereas Delhivery continues to operate at a larger scale in terms of express parcels and part truckload (PTL) transport.

Revenue Growth: Shadowfax Maintains a Faster Growth Trajectory
Shadowfax reported revenue from operations of Rs. 1,538 crore in Q2FY27, registering a 56.6% year-on-year increase compared with Rs. 982 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue also increased 13.2% sequentially from Rs. 1,358 crore in Q1FY27. The company highlighted that it had maintained more than 55% year-on-year revenue growth for six consecutive quarters, indicating sustained business momentum.
Advertisment
Express services remained the largest contributor, generating revenue of Rs. 1,096 crore, up 55.2% year-on-year. Hyperlocal revenue increased 87.7% to Rs. 341 crore, supported by demand from quick commerce and food delivery. Other logistics services contributed Rs. 100 crore.
Delhivery, meanwhile, reported revenue from services of approximately Rs. 3,017 crore in Q2FY27, compared with Rs. 2,536 crore in Q2FY26. Its transport business, comprising express parcel and PTL services, generated revenue of Rs. 2,633 crore, registering 22.1% growth. This indicates that Delhivery continues to operate at a considerably larger revenue base, while Shadowfax is currently recording faster growth.
Profitability: Both Companies Reported Improvement
Shadowfax reported a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs. 68 crore in Q2FY27, compared with Rs. 13 crore in the year-ago quarter, representing an increase of approximately 422%. Its PAT margin improved to 4.4%, compared with 1.3% in Q2FY26. This improvement reflects the company's ability to translate higher shipment volumes into stronger earnings.

Its adjusted EBITDA increased 177.4% year-on-year to Rs. 77 crore, compared with Rs. 28 crore in Q2FY26. The adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 5%, an improvement of approximately 218 basis points. The company attributed the improvement to operating leverage and growth across its business segments. It also reported an Ind AS EBITDA of Rs. 104 crore, with a margin of 6.7%.
Delhivery reported a PAT of Rs. 41 crore in Q2FY27, compared with a loss of Rs. 51 crore in Q2FY26. Its adjusted EBITDA increased to Rs. 123 crore from Rs. 83 crore, while the adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 4% from 3.3%. However, the comparison requires context: Delhivery disclosed that its Q2FY26 PAT, excluding the impact of the Ecom Express acquisition, was Rs. 59 crore. Therefore, the reported year-on-year PAT improvement does not necessarily indicate an improvement in underlying profitability against the comparable base.
Shipment Volumes: Demand Remains Strong Across Segments
Shadowfax delivered 27.1 crore orders during Q2FY27, registering 69.7% year-on-year growth. Express orders increased 72% to 21.7 crore, while Hyperlocal orders grew 63% to 5.4 crore. The company stated that customers are increasingly prioritising delivery speed, supporting demand for its express and same-day delivery services.

Delhivery handled 325 million express parcel shipments during the quarter, compared with 246 million in Q2FY26, representing 32.1% growth. Its PTL freight tonnage increased 14.2% to 545,000 metric tonnes. PTL freight revenue grew 23.1% to Rs. 672 crore, while express parcel revenue increased 21.7% to Rs. 1,961 crore.
The volume numbers indicate that both companies are benefiting from higher logistics demand. However, Shadowfax reported stronger growth in its disclosed order volumes, while Delhivery continues to handle substantial shipment volumes across its established transportation network.
Expansion Strategy: Different Growth Engines
Shadowfax is currently focused on four major growth engines, which include quick commerce and dark stores, Prime D2C deliveries, SMEs via Shadowfax 360, and Prime Large for bulky and volumetric deliveries. The company offers last-mile delivery services in more than 4,200 quick-commerce dark stores. The number of dark stores has increased from 47 stores in Q1FY27 to over 70 in Q2FY27, with a target of reaching above 100 stores by FY27.

The Prime D2C business delivered a revenue growth of around 2.1 times in year-over-year terms, offering same-day and next-day delivery services in more than 120 cities. Shadowfax 360 has also added more than 6,700 transacting sellers in the first two quarters of its launch, catering to small and medium enterprises.
Delhivery's growth story is based on its existing express parcel and PTL network. In Q2FY27, Delhivery saw growth in its parcel shipments and freight tonnage in the transport business. It also witnessed growth in its express delivery center network from 4,420 in Q2FY27 as against 3,863 in Q2FY26. The diversified service offering provides access to multiple logistics verticals instead of being dependent on one.

Cash Position and Financial Flexibility
For Shadowfax, as of September 2026, the company reported total cash and bank balances of approximately Rs. 1,562 crore, with no borrowings, thereby giving the company financial leverage to fuel its growth plans. Its investments in middle-mile infrastructure, technology and delivery have been made in order to increase efficiencies and volume capacity.
Delhivery, on the other hand, reported total cash and cash equivalents of Rs. 4,676 crore, and had no borrowings. The company's cash reserves give it the financial leverage to expand its network and make any required investments in technology. However, the company's lease liabilities were at approximately Rs. 1,465 crore.
Which Company Has the Stronger Growth Outlook?
Shadowfax has shown a faster growth in both revenue and shipment growth, together with a positive change in margins as adjusted EBITDA and PAT. Shadowfax has a number of growth opportunities with its quick commerce, D2C, and SME logistics businesses.
Delhivery, however, has a large operating base, has built its logistics network and has a lot of cash. The transport segment of Delhivery has been growing and making profits through the growth in express parcel and PTL segments.
From an investor’s perspective, the difference between the two companies becomes clear that is Shadowfax has better growth prospects and margin growth, while Delhivery has a better logistics network. Investors have to consider the valuations and management capability to make a decision about the better investment.
